access_method: Public page reader; not an authenticated DrivenData account or a submission-page receipt. Values may change after observation.

observations: Prediction target is geological faults, not confirmed geothermal vents.
Distance-weighted Tversky uses alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, and a triangular kernel with 300 m support.
Submission is one float32 GeoTIFF layer with confidence values in [0,1], EPSG:32611, 100 m resolution and the training bounds; the page says data outside the bounds are null or NaN.
The sample submission is described as predicting total fault absence.
The public and private test labels consist of expert-identified new faults; the final round uses expanded labels.

The GeoDAWN release provides magnetic and radiometric grids and line data for geological mapping; variable flight height and processing require attention when interpreting edges. The page identifies the release as CC0.
The public INGENIOUS compilation includes geothermal and geophysical datasets and is listed under CC BY 4.0; local download and exact geographic coverage were not verified here.
